articles.title: Brain wiring patterns linked to harm avoidance in obsessive-compulsive disorder
articles.summary: Researchers have linked denser nerve connections deep within the brain to a heightened sensitivity to potential threats. This specific brain wiring pattern appears across multiple psychiatric conditions, including obsessive-compulsive disorder and anxiety.

articles.title: PPDL: LLM-Based Flows as Probabilistic Programs
articles.summary: arXiv:2608.05234v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Building reliable applications that leverage large language models (LLMs) remains a significant challenge. While LLMs offer impressive capabilities across diverse tasks, their outputs often lack accuracy and provide no clear measure of confidence. This uncertainty compounds in flows of multiple calls to LLMs and other tools, making it difficult for developers and end-users to trust the results. articles.title: Decoupling Perception from Description: Computation-Grounded Representation Alignment between Multivariate Time Series and Language
articles.summary: arXiv:2608.05238v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Training multimodal models to align time series with language runs into a self-supervision trap. The usual recipe asks an LLM to read a series and write a description, so label quality is capped by the perceptual skill the model is supposed to learn. The data can never teach more than the labeler already knows. articles.title: The ethics of artificial intelligence in the life sciences: Universality, cultural diversity and an architecture of care
articles.summary: arXiv:2608.05436v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The life sciences and health research have started to benefit from artificial intelligence, which raises ethical concerns that are real but, we argue, not special. Any science should be governed by values that rest on how the human brain is built and socialised rather than anything distinct to artificial intelligence. Importantly, the human brain has a different, much less costly computational architecture than these machines. articles.title: Dark personality traits linked to problematic social media use via jealousy and cyberstalking
articles.summary: A new study suggests that for people with dark personality traits, problematic social media use is often tied to relationship jealousy. For these individuals, compulsive scrolling frequently involves suspicious thoughts and cyberstalking their romantic partners.

articles.summary: arXiv:2608.05481v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Hierarchical predictive coding proposes a compelling hypothesis of brain computation, suggesting that the cortex builds layered predictions to minimize surprise. Here, we examine a biologically plausible framework in which the functional goals of predictive coding emerge from local contrastive learning and simple activity cancellation. articles.title: Wearable ultrasound patch boosts REM sleep without drugs or surgery
articles.summary: A new wearable patch may help people reach REM sleep faster and remain there longer without medication or surgery. In a study of 28 participants, the device shortened the time to REM by 43 minutes and extended it by about 16 minutes. Researchers also observed signs of improved stress regulation and changes in brain circuits tied to emotion.

articles.title: Scientists discover a hidden brain shift that begins around age 50
articles.summary: Beginning around age 50, the brain’s memory center appears to lose many of its longtime immune cells and replace them with more inflammatory ones. This surprising shift may help explain how normal aging sets the stage for Alzheimer’s disease and dementia.

articles.title: Parental conservatism does not improve the transmission of religious beliefs, study shows
articles.summary: Young adults are more likely to share their parents' religious habits if they view their upbringing as warm but structured. A recent study reveals that regional geographic culture alters how different parenting strategies shape this intergenerational transmission of faith.

articles.title: Psilocybin therapy sessions for PTSD are mostly silent, study finds
articles.summary: New research indicates that psilocybin treatment for PTSD involves very little talking. Instead of traditional psychotherapy, data suggests patients benefit most from the quiet, unobtrusive presence of support staff.

articles.title: Scientists tracked 12 people in Antarctica for 10 months—what happened could shape future Mars missions
articles.summary: A ten-month Antarctic experiment found that astronauts may struggle not only with loneliness but also with spending too much time around the same people. Frequent contact was linked to greater tension and mistrust, while the crew increasingly divided into cultural and language-based groups.

articles.title: New autism therapy shows surprising benefits even in adult mice
articles.summary: Blocking the glycine transporter SLC6A20 restored important brain signaling and improved social, communication, and repetitive behaviors in autism-related mouse models. The treatment also worked in human brain organoids and showed lasting effects in adult mice, suggesting the brain may remain more treatable later in life than previously thought.

articles.title: Stopping ADHD medication alters sleep rhythms long after discontinuation
articles.summary: Stopping the common ADHD medication methylphenidate may cause lasting sleep disruptions. A new animal study reveals that rats experience fragmented rest and altered circadian rhythms ten days after ceasing the drug, highlighting potential long-term withdrawal effects.
